clue.text: Fear operating in theatre?

blocks.note: surface reading: a surgeon's nerves at work in the operating theatre
setter's reading: the dread that grips an actor performing on a theatre's boards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating theatre' pulls you towards surgery; split it and 'operating' just means at work, in a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the nervousness performers suffer before or during a show in front of an audience.

clue.text: Person seeking conflict resolution causes one to reach for hanky?

definitions.text: causes one to reach for hanky?
definitions.note: a cryptic second definition: a gun shooting at trouble, i.e. firing tear gas at a riot

blocks.note: first meaning: a fixer brought in to settle disputes or problems

blocks.clueFragment: causes one to reach for hanky?
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: a weapon aimed at a riot that fires tear gas and sets eyes streaming

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a riot-control gun shooting at trouble releases tear gas, so bystanders reach for handkerchiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is a mediator or problem-solver employed to sort out disputes and faults.

clue.text: Golf — I lost

blocks.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A golfer laments a lost ball, or a lost round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lost has disappeared, which is the adjective sense of the word.

clue.text: Escape taking in an elevated window

indicators.note: taking in means one word absorbs another inside itself

blocks.note: flight is the act of fleeing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner flees through a high window.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the small window set above a door, often semicircular, so it sits up high.

clue.text: Popular worker being dealt with

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A well-liked employee is the one handling the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in hand is under control and currently being attended to.

clue.text: Song that man mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the pronoun

blocks.note: that man is him, which is pronounced identically to a church song

explanation.surface: Someone refers to a song that a particular man sang.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise sung in church.

clue.text: Curious pleasure trip on Saturn, for example

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the following letters are made strange by rearranging them

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange space jaunt to Saturn, or perhaps an odd sightseeing outing with the Roman god.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call any planet orbiting further from the Sun than Earth a superior planet; Saturn is one example.

clue.text: End of exciting race, still perfect

blocks.note: a still is a single photograph, as opposed to moving film
to perfect something is to finish or polish it

explanation.surface: A race reaches its climax, and the ending is described as quite perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the noun for a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo finish is so close that a camera must decide the winner, the most thrilling ending a race can have.

clue.text: Sad having swallowed a chick, it seems?

definitions.text: having swallowed a chick, it seems?

blocks.note: first meaning: miserable, dejected

blocks.clueFragment: having swallowed a chick, it seems?
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: with a young bird's fluffy feathers literally in one's gob

explanation.walkthrough: Down is also the soft fluff of a chick, so a literal mouthful of it fits the whimsical second half.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone looking glum or dejected, with the corners of the lips turned downward.

clue.text: Fruit ending in tin, on average around about fifty

indicators.note: ending in points to just the final letter of the following word
around about suggests things being turned and moved about, so the collected letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of tin
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Tinned fruit tends to cost around fifty pence, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A navel orange is a seedless variety with a small secondary fruit forming a navel-like bump at one end.

clue.text: All kicking off in alley, some bully out for bad-boy tag?

indicators.note: kicking off means starting, and all of them means the start of each word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A thug causing trouble in a back street ends up branded a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO (Anti-Social Behaviour Order) was a British court order restricting a nuisance's conduct, and having one became a badge of yobbishness.
explanation.definitionFit: The order was slapped on unruly youths, so it served as a label marking someone out as a bad lad.

clue.text: Demon discovery with buried treasure, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the preceding word is wanted
something buried is hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a discovery is a find
the final letter of treasure

explanation.surface: A treasure hunter unearths a buried chest and finds a devil inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit or devil, a synonym of demon.

clue.text: One side walked out

blocks.note: first meaning: the side opposite right
second meaning: departed, past tense of leave

explanation.surface: One team quit the match in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a direction or side and the past tense of the verb meaning to depart.

clue.text: Horse stock last seen in cavalry

indicators.note: last seen in asks for only the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to stock shelves is to fill them
the final letter of cavalry

explanation.surface: A horse from the bloodstock was last spotted among the mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A filly is a young female horse.

clue.text: Sweets also found in outskirts of city

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept
found in says one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of city
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Sweet shops are also located on the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or confectionery.

clue.text: Ability to look all right in rowing team

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: yes means all right, as an assent
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's vision is in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, the power to look at things.

clue.text: Jack provided feedback at the outset, seeing charge list

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: Jack tar is an old name for a sailor, and both words mean seaman
if means provided that
the first letter of feedback

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack gave early comments after looking at a price list.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a published schedule of charges or duties.

clue.text: Most important king, perhaps, in a line

blocks.note: a king is one example of a playing card
taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The chief monarch stands in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of chief or fundamental importance, as in cardinal sin.

clue.text: Being worn, clutch to be dealt with later

blocks.note: clothes being worn are on
to clutch is to hold

explanation.surface: A worn clutch bag waits to be dealt with later, or a car's worn clutch awaits repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on hold has been postponed, set aside for attention at a later time.

clue.text: Tongue that's segmented

blocks.note: first meaning: the chief language of China
second meaning: a small citrus fruit that breaks into segments

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' means a language here, not the body part; the second half describes a fruit by its segments.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is both the main Chinese language and a small easy-peeling citrus fruit made of segments.

clue.text: Cash in, some counterfeit

indicators.note: counterfeit means fake or forged, so the letters are reworked into a false arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pays in banknotes, some of them forged.
explanation.definitionFit: Monies is a formal plural of money, meaning sums of cash.

clue.text: PM's predecessor certainly out of control

blocks.note: the morning hours, AM, come before the afternoon, PM
OK as an assent, meaning certainly

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister certainly lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' suggests a Prime Minister, but here it is the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means behaving wildly and uncontrollably.

clue.text: Bill featuring in play, sycophant

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within something, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to toy with is to play with
a bill is a poster, an advertisement, abbreviated to ad

explanation.surface: A character called Bill appears in a stage play as a flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is someone who fawns on the powerful, a synonym for sycophant.

clue.text: Not entirely unusual, a scandal I'm afraid to say

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Regrettably, a scandal is not entirely out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an expression of regret, used just as one says 'I'm afraid to say' before bad news.

clue.text: African country remaining

blocks.note: first meaning: the West African state
second meaning: two words, still left to be done

explanation.surface: An African nation is what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a nation in West Africa, and to go describes what is still outstanding.

clue.text: Simple building discarded

blocks.note: first meaning: a basic hut in the garden
second meaning: cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A basic hut has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a plain outbuilding, and shed is also the past tense of the verb meaning to cast off.

clue.text: Silly charging a tenor for old song

indicators.note: silly means foolish or crazy, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It is foolish to bill a tenor for performing an ancient song.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian chant is medieval plainsong of the Western Church, an old form of sung liturgy.

clue.text: Unite political party, terribly isolated

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the word before it is arranged badly, into a new order

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, the British right-of-centre party
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A party that feels terribly cut off tries to bring itself together.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate is to combine several things into one stronger whole, a synonym of unite.
